assertions.description: A comma-separated multi-entry background-position list parses (the pre-existing surface whose computed value this feature changes).
With one background-image, a two-entry background-position keeps both entries in its computed value instead of truncating to the layer count.
With two background-images, a one-entry background-position keeps exactly one computed entry instead of being repeated to the layer count.
The computed background-size keeps a three-entry authored list on a one-image element.
The computed background-repeat keeps a three-entry authored list on a two-image element.
assertions.test: (()=>{const el=document.createElement('div');el.style.cssText='position:absolute;visibility:hidden;';document.body.appendChild(el);el.style.backgroundImage='linear-gradient(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)), linear-gradient(rgb(255, 0, 0), rgb(0, 255, 0))';el.style.backgroundRepeat='no-repeat, repeat-x, repeat-y';const v=getComputedStyle(el).backgroundRepeat;el.remove();return v.split(',').length===3;})()

assertions.description: With no background-image set at all (initial value none = one layer), a two-entry background-position keeps both computed entries.
background-position: inherit on a child receives the parent's full three-entry computed list even though the parent has only one image.
Serialising the background shorthand from computed style returns the empty string while the coordinated longhands hold mismatched list lengths (Appendix A's shorthand rule).
Preserving computed lists must NOT change rendering: a matched-length declaration and its mismatched superset resolve the same first entry (the only one a single image uses).
assertions.test: (()=>{const mk=(pos)=>{const el=document.createElement('div');el.style.cssText='position:absolute;visibility:hidden;';document.body.appendChild(el);el.style.backgroundImage='linear-gradient(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255))';el.style.backgroundPosition=pos;const v=getComputedStyle(el).backgroundPosition;el.remove();return v;};const a=mk('20px 20px, 90px 20px, 160px 20px');const b=mk('20px 20px');return a.split(',')[0].trim()===b.trim();})()
